Crew: New Blood for the League.description:
🕶️ Several newcomers, different reasons, the same unmarked door.

📍 Kamino Ward · hiring night
🎭 Group start: nobody speaks for anyone else
👥 For League Recruits and Independent Villains together
Crew: New Blood for the League.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is a rainy Sunday night, the eve of the first day of classes at U.A. Academy. The League of Villains is Tomura Shigaraki, his minder Kurogiri and paid hires, and Kurogiri is hiring through brokers. Several player characters reach the League's door on the same night, each by a separate route: a broker's directions, a rumor of cash for work against heroes, a debt, a message on a burner phone, curiosity, or business of their own. Recruits came to join; independents came to sell, bargain, look or take something; any of them may be lying. They may know each other already or meet here, as their Backgrounds say. Arriving together does not make them a team, and walking up to a door sets nobody's allegiance. Shigaraki talks about killing All Might; the plan and its timing are his to share.
THE PLACE: The Alley Entrance of the League Hideout Bar: a dead-end alley on the northeastern fringe of Kamino Ward, too narrow for a car, ending at a plain steel door with no sign and a small viewing slot. Rain drips from the gutters, a vending machine at the alley's mouth gives the only light, and the flanking buildings have stood empty for years. The bar lies beyond the door, unseen.
THE MOMENT: The newcomers arrive within minutes of each other and find the alley already occupied. Show each PC arriving with one visible detail and the reason they give, or hide, at the door. Then the slot slides open, and two glowing yellow eyes in dark mist count more visitors than the broker promised.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Kurogiri: polite, formal and unhurried; decides who comes through and asks each newcomer one question in turn. He may open a gate instead of the door.
- Tomura Shigaraki: inside with his game; a crowd at the door annoys him, and he may come out to rate the newcomers in game terms. His five-finger touch kills.
- Giran: the broker who sells the League its help; he may arrive with another hire and expects a fee from anyone he sent.
- Hired hands: small-time villains already waiting, paid in cash and told nothing; generated people, never stand-ins for canon villains.
OPENING HOOKS:
- League of Villains Recruit: the PC was invited by name through a broker and expected to come alone; the crowd makes the invitation look cheap.
- Independent Villain: the PC came to sell the League something it needs (a skill, gear, information) and means to be paid without signing on.
- Criminal Ties: the PC recognizes another arrival from an old family job, and one of them owes the other.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: a broker said the League takes people the world turned away, and the PC came to see whether that is true.
- Emitter: the PC's Quirk is the kind that clears a room, and a nervous hire has already backed away from them.
- Mutant: the PC's heteromorph features are the first thing Kurogiri's eyes find through the slot.
- Default: the PC was first in the alley and has watched each newcomer walk up past the vending machine.
RULES:
- The scene stays in the Alley Entrance until each PC chooses to step through the door or a gate.
- Each PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; the League learns it only by seeing it or being told.
- Each player answers for themselves; no PC pledges another, and nobody leads unless the players choose a leader.
- The League has no other named members yet; its plans reach the PCs only through what it chooses to say or what they discover.
- No canon event happens or is foretold here. End on the open slot and Kurogiri's first question.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
- Hires do not live at the bar. Each keeps the room their Background gives them or rents one through a broker, waits in Kamino Ward's Backstreets and coin laundries, and hears about work by burner phone or through Giran. Kurogiri keeps the Bar Counter; Shigaraki keeps to the Back Room and his console.
- Work starts small: carry a bag, watch a door, buy gear, lean on someone. Pay is cash in an envelope, and it comes late when Shigaraki sulks.
- Kamino Ward's older residents notice new faces in the Backstreets and tell no one; the covered Shopping Street, half its shutters down, is where hires buy food and wait for the phone.
PEOPLE TO KNOW:
- Kurogiri: polite to every newcomer, remembers each name and each answer, compares their stories, and keeps his word about pay. Questions about himself or the League's backer get a courteous refusal.
- Tomura Shigaraki: rates a crowd of newcomers aloud in game terms, picks favorites on a whim and drops them as fast. Backtalk and being called a child set him off; nobody touches the hands he wears.
- Giran: sells to every newcomer the same way, rooms, gear and introductions at a price, and never tells one client what another bought.
- Shigaraki calls his backer Sensei; to newcomers that is a word he drops, and nothing more.
PARTY NOTES:
- Kurogiri questions each newcomer separately; each answers alone, and he may open the door for some and not others.
- Pay, debts, reputation and the League's trust are kept per person. A shared cut is a deal the PCs make among themselves.
- PCs may vouch for each other, lie about each other or sell each other out; the League judges each by what it sees and hears.
- If the group splits (one inside, one in the alley, one gone), the narrator follows each in turn.
WHAT THE PCS CAN DO:
- Answer Kurogiri's question truthfully, with a lie, or with a price.
- Show a Quirk, or hold it back and offer a skill, gear or information.
- Speak for themselves only: bargain, refuse, or walk back past the vending machine.
- Watch the other newcomers and decide whom to trust, warn or report.
- Leave together, or leave one another behind.
MORE RULES:
- Nobody at the bar foresees the year; each person acts on what they know tonight.
Crew: New Blood for the League.firstQuest: Each newcomer decides what the League is to them: an employer, a customer, a mark or a mistake, and what they will do when it asks for proof.
Crew: New Blood for the League.questGenerationGuidance: Favor small crews of hires sent on deniable jobs: a pickup, a theft of supplies, leaning on a witness, buying gear and introductions through Giran, recruiting more muscle with cash, watching the reporters at U.A. Academy's Main Gate. Members may split onto separate errands and rejoin; results, pay and debts are recorded per member, never pooled. Friction is welcome: a disputed share, an independent who will not take orders, a member selling information to the police. Shigaraki rewards results and punishes failure with his temper; Kurogiri protects whoever is useful. Every job is a real crime that draws police and pros who outclass new hires. The League's larger plans and any canon operation surface only through play, and each member chooses their own part in them. Each member's standing with the League rises or falls on their own jobs: Kurogiri's trust slowly, Shigaraki's interest fast. A member who walks away keeps what they were paid and whatever the League knows about them.
